title: India Women Open Asian Games Title Defence Against Japan in Cricket Quarter-Final
excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's defending champions face hosts Japan in the first-ever women's T20I between the sides, with the winner advancing to Saturday's semi-final against Bangladesh.
body:
• Defending champions India began their Asian Games 2026 title defence on Friday, facing hosts Japan in the women's cricket quarter-final at Korogi Athletic Park, Nisshin.
  • Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss and opted to field; Kranti Gaud opened the bowling for India in the first-ever T20I between the two women's sides.
  • The match is being broadcast on the Sony Sports Network and DD Sports, with live streaming on SonyLIV — starting 10:30 AM IST (2:00 PM JST).
  • A win sends India into Saturday's semi-final against Bangladesh, with the gold-medal match on Tuesday; if rain washes the game out, higher-ranked India advance automatically.

Title defence begins

India's women began their Asian Games 2026 campaign on Friday with a quarter-final against hosts Japan at the Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin, Aichi — a day before the Games' official opening ceremony. Harmanpreet Kaur's side, the defending champions after winning gold at Hangzhou 2023 by beating Sri Lanka by 19 runs, won the toss and chose to field first, with Kranti Gaud opening the bowling attack.

It is the first-ever T20 international between the India and Japan women's teams, and the mismatch on paper is stark: India sit third in the ICC women's T20I rankings; Japan are 39th. Under the Asian Games' playing conditions, India would advance even if the match is washed out, with the higher-ranked side progressing — the same rule applied at the 2022 edition.

India XI: Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Harmanpreet Kaur (c), G Kamalini, Bharti Fulmali, Richa Ghosh (w), Deepti Sharma, Shree Charani, Shreyanka Patil, Kranti Gaud, Nandani Sharma.
Japan XI: Haruna Iwasaki, Akari Nishimura Kano (w), Mai Yanagida (c), Erika Oda, Ahilya Chandel, Shimako Kato, Ayaka Kato-Stafford, Ayumi Fujikawa, Hinase Goto, Erika Toguchi Quinn, Nonoha Yasumoto.

How to watch

The match is being broadcast live in India on the Sony Sports Network — with coverage across Sony Sports Ten 1, 2, 3 (Hindi) and Ten 4 (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada) — and is also available on free-to-air DD Sports. Live streaming is on the SonyLIV app and website. In Japan, TBS Television carries the broadcast; other broadcasters include PTV Sports (Pakistan), i-CABLE and HOY TV (Hong Kong) and beIN Sports (MENA).

A landmark fixture for Japanese cricket

For Japan, the quarter-final is a landmark in its own right. Hosting cricket at a home Asian Games gives the sport rare visibility in a country where it remains a niche pursuit — but one the Japan Cricket Association has grown steadily, with a women's national side competing in ICC pathway events and a domestic league feeding the national setup. Japan's cricket moment dovetails with the game's broader push toward the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where cricket returns after a 128-year absence. For the hosts, sharing a field with the world No. 3 side is the payoff for years of quiet development work — and a showcase for a sport Japan wants to take seriously.

The road to gold

The women's tournament runs on a straight knockout format from the quarter-final stage, with the top seeds entering directly. Should India beat Japan, they face Bangladesh in the second semi-final on Saturday. Win that, and the likely gold-medal match on Tuesday pits them against the winner of Sri Lanka or Pakistan's semi-final — a potential India-Pakistan final. A semi-final defeat would drop India into the bronze-medal match, also on Tuesday.

India and Pakistan currently share the record for most Asian Games cricket golds, with two each. For India, the quarter-final is expected to be the gentlest test of the tournament — the real examination starts Saturday.
